title: Order-intake stock-and-flow backlog model
purpose: Represent a bounded intake queue as a stock with admission, service and rejection flows so that conservation, capacity and backlog behavior can be checked before a discrete-event model is attempted.

includes: A single request class arriving at a declared rate
A service capacity derived from servers and mean service time
Exact request conservation across completed, rejected and backlog states

abstraction.boundary: The intake boundary starts when a request is offered and ends when it is completed, rejected or left in backlog at the horizon.
abstraction.resolution: Fixed-step fluid integration. Individual requests are not represented; the model is intentionally coarser than the discrete-event model.

state_variables.name: backlog
state_variables.description: Requests admitted but not yet served.

state_variables.name: rejected
state_variables.description: Cumulative offered requests refused because admission capacity was full.

parameters.name: arrival_rate
parameters.note: Synthetic offered load. It is not a measured arrival rate.

parameters.name: service_mean
parameters.note: Synthetic mean service time. It is not a measured service-time distribution.

parameters.name: servers
parameters.note: Configured service capacity; not a measured deployment size.

parameters.name: queue_capacity
parameters.note: Admission bound used to model backpressure.

parameters.name: cost_per_server_hour
parameters.note: Synthetic relative cost used only for business-comparable comparison.

equations: served(t) = min(backlog(t) + admitted(t), servers / service_mean * dt)

invariants.name: request-conservation
invariants.statement: At every step, offered requests equal completed plus rejected plus backlog within floating-point tolerance.

invariants.name: non-negative-backlog
invariants.statement: Backlog never becomes negative and service never exceeds available work.

invariants.name: capacity-admission
invariants.statement: Admission stops when the configured queue capacity is reached.
invariants.check: rejected > 0 when offered load exceeds capacity

cases.description: Deterministic arrivals below service capacity produce zero rejection and non-growing backlog.
Offered load above admission capacity produces rejections and conserves requests.
Zero arrivals and zero servers leave all stocks at zero.

verification.notes: These checks prove only the implemented fluid accounting and the exercised boundary cases. They do not validate the model against a real intake system.

evidence.note: Synthetic rate, not a measured arrival process.
Synthetic mean, not a measured service-time distribution.
Configured candidate capacity, not a measured deployment.
Configured admission bound, not a measured buffer.

calibration.notes: No production data were used. All numbers are synthetic and exist only to exercise the model contract.

validity_limits: Valid only for the synthetic offered load, service capacity and admission bound recorded in a scenario.
The fluid approximation ignores individual request latency, retries and timeout ordering.
No claim is made about a real intake system, capacity plan or service-level objective.
assumptions: A single request class is sufficient for the bounded comparison.
Service capacity is constant over the horizon.
Admission is first-come and rejects when the configured backlog limit is reached.
unknowns: The real arrival distribution and its correlation with business events.
The real service-time distribution and its tail behavior.
The operational cost of queueing and rejection.
